title: Plus One
corePattern: Right-to-Left Array Simulation with Carry Propagation
interviewTips: Ask if input can be empty and if leading zeros are possible, and whether to modify in-place or return new array
Trade-off: converting to integer overflows for large n, while digit-by-digit simulation is O(n) and safe for arbitrary length
Edge-case tip: all 9s like [9,9,9] requires growing array to [1,0,0,0] - handle carry out of most significant digit

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force - Right-to-Left Carry Simulation
approaches.intuition: Add one like in elementary school: start at last digit, if it is less than 9 just increment and finish, otherwise set to 0 and carry to the left. If carry falls off the front, prepend 1.
approaches.theory: Digits are big-endian base-10. Adding 1 affects only a suffix of trailing 9s. We propagate carry leftwards: digits[i] = (digits[i] + carry) % 10, carry = (digits[i] + carry) // 10. Since initial increment is 1, we can early exit on first non-9. If every digit was 9, mathematical result needs n+1 digits: 1 followed by n zeros.

timeComplexity.explanation: Worst case scan all n digits once when input is all 9s, best case O(1) when last digit is not 9.

spaceComplexity.explanation: In-place update using O(1) extra space, excluding O(n) output for new array only in all-9s overflow case.

steps: i=2: digits[2]=3 < 9, increment to 4 and return

approaches.name: Approach 2: Optimal - Rightmost Non-Nine Pivot
approaches.intuition: Only trailing 9s become 0. Find the rightmost digit that is not 9, increment it once, and zero everything to its right. If no such digit exists, the number was 10^n - 1.
approaches.theory: Let k be index of last non-9. Then result = prefix[0..k-1] + (digits[k]+1) + zeros(k+1..n-1). This is mathematically equivalent to addition with carry but separates the search phase from the write phase, making correctness obvious and minimizing writes to exactly the suffix. If k = -1, answer is 1 followed by n zeros.

timeComplexity.explanation: One backward scan to find pivot plus one forward zeroing of trailing 9s, at most 2n steps so linear.

spaceComplexity.explanation: O(1) auxiliary space in-place, O(n) output only when all digits are 9.

steps: scan from right: i=2,1,0 all 9, so i becomes -1
